name: setup_rt_frame32
prose: Builds a 32-bit rt signal frame for ksig on the user stack and returns 0 or a nonzero error. It calls synchronize_user_stack() and save_and_clear_fpu(), reads wsaved with get_thread_wsaved(), and computes sigframe_size from sizeof(*sf), adding __siginfo_fpu_t if fpsaved[0] has FPRS_FEF and __siginfo_rwin_t if wsaved is nonzero. It takes sf from get_sigframe; if invalid_frame_pointer(sf, sigframe_size) is true it optionally logs, calls force_sigsegv(ksig->sig) and returns -EINVAL (registers not yet modified). Otherwise, if TIF_32BIT is set it truncates regs->tpc and regs->tnpc to 32 bits (the registers are modified from this point on) and then stores the saved state into the frame with put_user/__put_user: pc, npc, y, psr (with PSR_EF if the FPU state is saved), the 16 u_regs, the v8plus extension words and ASI, the FPU state (fpu_save pointer or 0), and, if wsaved is nonzero, the register-window state, setting set_thread_wsaved(0); it also stores the siginfo, alternate stack, signal mask and either a copy of the register window at the old frame pointer (when wsaved is 0) or the saved window from reg_window[wsaved - 1]. Errors are accumulated by OR into err, and if err is nonzero it returns err at that point, after tpc/tnpc truncation and (when wsaved was nonzero) clearing of wsaved. It then sets UREG_FP to sf, I0 to the signal number, I1 to &sf->info, I2 to &sf->regs, sets regs->tpc to the handler address and tnpc to tpc + 4 (truncated to 32 bits if TIF_32BIT), and sets I7 to the restorer if there is one; otherwise it points I7 into the frame's insns, writes the two trampoline instructions with __put_user (returning err if that fails) and calls flush_signal_insns. It returns 0 on success.

Reviewer 15 (on write error tpc/tnpc may already be truncated and wsaved cleared) RIGHT: signal32.c:523-526,557,582-583. Slice cut head; real function at 487-621.

name: do_mathemu
prose: SPARC64 FPU-trap emulation. It returns 0 when it did not emulate the instruction and 1 when it emulated it successfully (or when a conditional fmovq condition is false and the instruction is turned into a nop), or the value of record_exception(regs, _fex) when the emulation raised FP exceptions (that helper was not read). If the trap came from privileged mode (TSTATE_PRIV) it calls die_if_kernel. It counts a software emulation event, truncates the pc to 32 bits if TIF_32BIT, and reads the instruction with get_user; if that fails it returns 0. It classifies the instruction as FPOP1 or FPOP2 by its opcode bits and sets type from a table of known operations (the ftt value expected, operand sizes and pack/unpack flags); for the conditional fmovq forms it evaluates the condition from %fsr or the condition codes: if false it clears the CEXC field of xfsr, sets tpc = tnpc, tnpc += 4 and returns 1, and if true it rewrites the instruction as a plain fmovq. Unrecognised opcodes leave type 0 and the function returns 0. If type is set: when illegal_insn_trap is false it requires the xfsr ftt field to equal the expected trap type, else it returns 0; then it clears the ftt field (&= ~0x1c000), decodes the source and destination FP registers (a quad register number with bit 1 set sets the invalid_fp_register trap type in xfsr and returns 0), unpacks the operands, performs the operation with the soft-float macros, and unless FP_INHIBIT_RESULTS stores the result in the destination register (or into the addressed fcc field of xfsr for compares). If _fex is nonzero it returns record_exception(regs, _fex); otherwise it clears the CEXC field of xfsr (FSR_CEXC_MASK), advances tpc = tnpc and tnpc += 4 and returns 1. When the destination register is written it also marks fpsaved (setting FPRS_FEF and zeroing the half of the register file that was not yet saved).

name: bpf_int_jit_compile
prose: Sparc64 BPF JIT entry point; returns the program to use (the JITed prog, or the original prog when JIT is not done or fails). It returns orig_prog at once if prog->jit_requested is false, and also if bpf_jit_blind_constants fails; if blinding returned a different program it is used (tmp_blinded). It uses prog->aux->jit_data, allocating it with kzalloc if NULL (failure: prog = orig_prog and return without the cleanup at out_off). If jit_data->ctx.offset is already set (an extra pass of a multi-function program) it reuses the saved ctx, image and header and jumps to the final pass. Otherwise it allocates ctx.offset (kmalloc_array; failure: orig_prog), then runs up to 39 passes of build_prologue/build_body/build_epilogue until the generated size stops changing (a build_body failure gives orig_prog); it allocates the image with bpf_jit_binary_alloc (failure: orig_prog). The final pass rebuilds the code into the image; a build_body failure or a size that differs from the previous pass frees the header and gives orig_prog. It flushes the icache, and, if the program is not a subprogram or this is the extra pass, makes the image read-only with bpf_jit_binary_lock_ro (failure: free header, orig_prog); otherwise it saves ctx, image and header in jit_data for the extra pass. It sets prog->bpf_func, jited and jited_len, and when finished (non-subprogram or extra pass) fills the jited line info and, at out_off, frees ctx.offset and jit_data and clears prog->aux->jit_data. At out, if constants were blinded it releases the unused one of the two programs with bpf_jit_prog_release_other. It returns prog.

name: prom_console_write_buf
prose: Writes len bytes of buf to the PROM console. It loops while len is nonzero: n = __prom_console_write_buf(buf, len); if n < 0 it retries with the same buf and len; otherwise it executes len -= n and then buf += len, that is, buf is advanced by the remaining length after the subtraction, not by n. It returns (void) only when len becomes exactly 0. A call that returns n == 0 leaves len unchanged but still moves buf forward by len; if n is greater than len, len becomes negative and the loop continues. So the pointer advance is not the number of bytes written.

name: port_open
prose: Opens a port channel. It waits for a connection with port_wait(data->kernel_data), giving fd. If fd >= 0 and data->raw is set, it calls tcgetattr(fd, &data->tt) (retrying on EINTR) and, if that returns nonzero, returns the error at once; then it calls raw(fd) and returns its error if nonzero; both of these error returns happen before *dev_out is written and the fd is not closed here. name: time_travel_ext_req
prose: Sends a time-travel request with opcode op and time to the external controller and waits for its ACK; it returns the msg.time value of the message. It increments the static sequence counter to get mseq, builds a struct um_timetravel_msg with op, time and seq, calls block_signals_hard(), and writes the message to time_travel_ext_fd with os_write_file (its result is not checked). If op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_WAIT and time_travel_shm is set it goes straight to unblocking (no ACK is read). Otherwise it loops calling time_travel_handle_message(&msg, ...) (mode TTMH_READ_START_ACK if op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_START, else TTMH_READ) until msg.op is UM_TIMETRAVEL_ACK; if the ACK's seq differs from mseq it calls panic. For UM_TIMETRAVEL_GET it then calls time_travel_set_time(msg.time). It calls unblock_signals_hard() and returns msg.time (the ACK's time, or the sent time in the shared-memory WAIT case).

How non-ACK messages are answered is inside time_travel_handle_message, which was not read, so the old claim about answering them with an ACK is dropped. Code at time.c:196-245. Slice cut head.

name: segv
prose: Handles a UML segmentation fault; it always returns 0 on its normal paths (panic paths do not return). If !is_user and regs is non-NULL it saves regs in current->thread.segv_regs. Branches: (1) !is_user and init_mm.context.sync_tlb_range_to set: um_tlb_sync(&init_mm); -ENOMEM calls report_enomem; any error panics; otherwise it goes to out. (2) current->pagefault_disabled: if mc is NULL it calls show_regs and panics; if thread.segv_continue is NULL it panics; otherwise it sets the mcontext rip to segv_continue, clears segv_continue and goes to out. (3) current->mm == NULL: panic. (4) !is_user and address strictly between PAGE_SIZE and TASK_SIZE: panic (kernel access to user memory). Otherwise, if SEGV_IS_FIXABLE(&fi) it calls handle_page_fault(address, ip, is_write, is_user, &si_code), else err = -EFAULT and address = 0. If err is 0 it goes to out; for a kernel fault (!is_user) arch_fixup(ip, regs) true also goes to out; a remaining kernel fault panics. For a user fault it calls show_segv_info(regs), records the faultinfo, and sends SIGBUS (BUS_ADRERR) if err == -EACCES, else BUG_ON(err != -EFAULT) and SIGSEGV with si_code via force_sig_fault. At out it clears current->thread.segv_regs if regs is non-NULL and returns 0. Several panic paths dereference regs through container_of without a NULL check (a NULL regs is only safe on the paths that do not use it).
note: Reviewer 2 (pagefault-disabled case recovers via segv_continue, panics only when it is missing) RIGHT: trap.c:332-344. Reviewer 15 (precondition wrongly excludes NULL regs for a user fault) RIGHT: user faults handled without dereferencing regs except through show_segv_info/arch paths. name: __wrap_free
prose: UML wrapper that frees a pointer according to where it was allocated; returns void. It takes addr = (unsigned long)ptr. If addr is in [uml_physmem, high_physmem) it calls kfree(ptr) only if kmalloc_ok is set; else if addr is in [start_vm, end_vm) it calls vfree(ptr) only if kmalloc_ok is set; otherwise (any other address) it calls __real_free(ptr). When kmalloc_ok is clear and the pointer lies in one of the first two regions, nothing is freed (the source comment notes possible leaks).

name: __add_sigio_fd
prose: Registers fd with the global epoll instance epollfd for edge-triggered input. It fills a struct epoll_event with data.fd = fd and events = EPOLLIN | EPOLLET, calls epoll_ctl(epollfd, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, fd, &event) retrying on EINTR, and returns 0 if that succeeded or -errno if it failed. prose: Queues a stub mmap for the child mm: map(mm_idp, virt, len, prot, phys_fd, offset), always returning 0. name: cts_cbc_encrypt
prose: AES-NI CBC-CTS encrypt for a skcipher request (aesni-intel_glue.c:243-297). It sets up a sub-request subreq with the same tfm and callback flags. cbc_blocks = DIV_ROUND_UP(req->cryptlen, 16) - 2. If req->cryptlen <= 16: a length below 16 returns -EINVAL, and a length of exactly 16 sets cbc_blocks = 1. If cbc_blocks > 0 it CBC-encrypts the first cbc_blocks blocks with cbc_encrypt(&subreq) (returning its error if nonzero); if req->cryptlen == 16 it then returns 0 (a one-block message is processed by CBC only, not by the ciphertext-stealing step); otherwise it advances src and dst past those blocks with scatterwalk_ffwd. It then sets up subreq for the remaining bytes (req->cryptlen - cbc_blocks * 16) and calls skcipher_walk_virt (returning its error if nonzero), runs aesni_cts_cbc_enc on the walk's buffers inside kernel_fpu_begin()/kernel_fpu_end(), and returns skcipher_walk_done(&walk, 0).

name: DEFINE_FREDENTRY_RAW(int80_emulation)
prose: Generated FRED entry function for the 32-bit INT $0x80 vector (named fred_int80_emulation by the macro; the packet listed it as do_int80_emulation_fred); returns void. Given regs, it calls enter_from_user_mode(regs), then instrumentation_begin() and add_random_kstack_offset(). It sets regs->orig_ax = regs->ax & GENMASK(31, 0) (the low 32 bits of the syscall number) and regs->ax = -ENOSYS, calls nr = syscall_32_enter(regs), enables interrupts with local_irq_enable(), calls nr = syscall_enter_from_user_mode_work(regs, nr), then do_syscall_32_irqs_on(regs, nr), instrumentation_end() and syscall_exit_to_user_mode(regs). Unlike do_int80_emulation it does not check user_mode() or int80_is_external(). The effects of syscall_32_enter and the other helpers (for example any thread-flag changes) are not described here because they were not read.

name: emulate_vsyscall
prose: Called from the x86 page-fault path to emulate a vsyscall; returns true if it handled the fault (including by sending a signal) and false if it did nothing. It returns false, without modifying regs, when (error_code & (X86_PF_WRITE | X86_PF_USER)) != X86_PF_USER; when address != regs->ip (a data access, with a warning unless vsyscall_mode is EMULATE); and when vsyscall_mode == NONE (with a warning). With NX it WARNs once if X86_PF_INSTR is not set. Then vsyscall_nr = addr_to_vsyscall_nr(address); a negative value, an unreadable user stack slot at regs->sp (get_user of the return address), or a failed write_ok_or_segv check of the user buffers for the call (gettimeofday: di and si; time: di; getcpu: di and si) jumps to sigsegv, which calls force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns true. Otherwise it sets regs->orig_ax = the real syscall number and regs->ax = -ENOSYS and calls secure_computing(); if seccomp changed the number or the ip it logs, calls force_exit_sig(SIGSYS) and returns true. It sets regs->orig_ax = -1; if secure_computing asked to skip the call it goes to do_ret (regs->ax remains -ENOSYS), otherwise it calls __x64_sys_gettimeofday, __x64_sys_time or __x64_sys_getcpu (for getcpu it temporarily sets regs->dx to 0 and restores it); a result of -EFAULT goes to sigsegv, any other result is stored in regs->ax. At do_ret it sets regs->ip to the saved return address (caller), adds 8 to regs->sp, and returns true.
